originalStory: Already mid-action, Pip the rabbit tries to place one sticky note on the toy cabinet's empty front panel, but it clings to Pip's fingertip while the cabinet stays untouched. Pip tries to peel the note away with the free hand, but it splits into two notes, one on each hand. Pip tries to press both notes onto the cabinet, but they spring back and double into four notes. Pip tries to push the four notes off against the cabinet door edge, but they split into eight and cover Pip's arms and face. Pip sees the four-to-eight change finish, realizes that every removal or transfer attempt multiplies the notes, deliberately stops struggling, and turns the still note-covered face toward the mirror. Pip remains covered until a sneeze scatters the notes onto the cabinet. Pip is relieved, but the cabinet remains messy.

storyRequestPreview.system: Return ONLY one JSON object matching this schema: {"alternatives":[{"candidateId":"candidate-1","title":"short title","text":"complete story"}]}. Return exactly the number of alternatives requested in context.requestedAlternativeCount (between 1 and 3). Each candidate must include a non-empty candidateId, title and text string. When returning multiple alternatives, each must have a meaningfully different narrative body — do not reuse the same story text with only a different title. Vary at least one of: action/progression strategy, how the central physical rule causes consequences, escalation structure, visual discovery, or permitted payoff. The user supplied input in mode context.inputMode (IDEA = short concept, DETAILED_STORY = complete narrative). Respect context.storyGenerationMode: for EXPLORE_DIFFERENT_STORIES generate meaningfully different narrative directions from the supplied idea; for IMPROVE_EXISTING_STORY refine the supplied narrative while preserving only the explicitly locked requirements listed in context.lockedRequirements. The locked requirements are: PRESERVE_CORE_PREMISE (keep the central concept), PRESERVE_KEY_EVENTS (keep the major events in order), PRESERVE_ENDING (keep the final outcome). Only the requirements present in context.lockedRequirements are binding; do not silently lock requirements that are absent. Preserve supplied characters and intent. Do not return markdown, reasoning, commentary or production authorization. Design observable narrative events that can later be expressed as source-bound production beats under Ruleset 1.11. The objective is a genuinely coherent story, not a manufactured numeric score. For short ABSURD_PHYSICS work, use distinct character problem-solving strategies only when they naturally advance the same central mechanic; pulling harder, repeating a pull, relabeling an action, or changing the camera are not distinct story strategies. Make active involvement, causal consequences, progression, and a realization/reversal/payoff explicit in the story text. Opening clarity, curiosity, suspense, discovery, and non-comedic payoffs are all valid. Never claim visual or audience evidence. Protected source changes remain proposals requiring owner approval; preserve the supplied character, core premise, physical rule, and ending. Improve the actual viewer-visible story, not hand positions or a rule checklist. Consider Instant Impossible, Immediate Problem and Curiosity/Discovery openings without requiring impossible physics in every concept. Seek distinct visible consequences, natural pacing, active character decisions and a causally earned payoff. Allow enough time for major events; do not pack realization, mirror reaction, scatter and resolution into the final seconds. Prefer clear silhouettes and direct interactions; identify thin-object/count/face continuity uncertainty rather than promising render success. Character identity and the existing physical rule are locked when PRESERVE_CHARACTER_IDENTITY or PRESERVE_PHYSICAL_RULE is supplied. Unlocked events may be proposed for revision, but no revision is applied until explicit owner approval.

details.recommendation: Distinct from CONCEPT_007: a single, internally consistent mechanic is not automatically a legible one. CHAR_002 confirms the character is active for enough of the runtime; this asks whether that activity reads as emotionally engaged and sympathetic rather than blank, robotic, aggressive, or stuck in prolonged panic. details.recommendation: Distinct from ATTEMPT_002 (semantic strategy diversity): ATTEMPT_002 asks whether the character is genuinely trying a different strategy; this asks whether that different strategy will actually LOOK different and be reliably executable by an image-to-video generation model (e.g. Seedance). A deterministic keyword pre-filter flags abstract-intent language ('blocks the escape route', 'tries to outsmart') and vague movement-magnitude phrasing ('slightly moves') on attempt beats, plus a beat-budget estimate (too many attempts for the available duration). An LLM semantic check (check_attempts_are_generation_executable) judges each attempt for a concrete action-result pair and flags attempts that would visually collapse into the same choreography despite different wording. BLOCKER only when NO attempt is judged executable at all or the LLM is unreachable (SERVICE_ERROR); CRITICAL when some attempts are unexecutable or abstract-intent language is matched; WARNING for vague magnitude phrasing or beat-budget pressure alone.
